description: Perimeter symmetry cluster (user <USER>), Slurm 21.08, every CPU partition OverSubscribe=EXCLUSIVE (whole nodes, no SU). amdq first (AMD EPYC 7532, 2 x 32 cores, 256 GB, NPS=4), defq as fallback (Intel Xeon Gold 6148, 2 x 20 cores, 191 GB); jobs that may run on either vendor list "amdq,defq" with --mem=180G and size workers inside the job. Rows are packed into whole nodes, one pinned process per CPU package.

grid.vendor_reason: AMD nodes have only 84 GB of node-local /local1 (measured on <NODE> and <NODE>), less than the grid needs (N=768: 122 GB, N=1024: 287 GB); Intel nodes have 568 GB (rotating disk). Alternatively copy the grid from Expanse with cluster/sitekit/transfer_grid.sh.

AMD nodes have only 84 GB of node-local /local1 (measured on <NODE> and <NODE>), less than the grid needs (N=768: 122 GB, N=1024: 287 GB); Intel nodes have 568 GB (rotating disk). Alternatively copy the grid from Expanse with cluster/sitekit/transfer_grid.sh.

profile_basis: Rows: from the Expanse pilot and the symmetry pilot (calibration below); rows run on either vendor (amdq,defq, --mem=180G) and are packed two per node (one numactl-pinned process per package) for N <= 768, one per node for N = 1024. Grids for N >= 768 need more node-local disk than the AMD nodes have (84 GB), so they run on Intel defq nodes (568 GB rotating /local1: the N=1024 generator writes and re-reads a 208 GB memory-mapped array, estimated 5-6 h, 12 h limit) or are copied from Expanse with cluster/sitekit/transfer_grid.sh. Projections assume the slower vendor; every job ends within half of the 24 h wall.
